chunks: And with this chain, from al-Hasan, from Sa'id, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever recites 'Alhakumut Takathur' in his obligatory prayer, Allah will write for him the reward of a hundred martyrs. And whoever recites it in his recommended prayer, Allah will write for him the reward of fifty martyrs. And forty rows of angels will pray with him in his obligatory prayer, if Allah wills.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Takathur in prayer?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith emphasizes the spiritual potency of Surah Al-Takathur, linking its recitation to the high status of martyrdom. The specific distinction between obligatory and voluntary prayers underscores the cumulative nature of devotional acts in Shia piety, while the presence of forty rows of angels signifies divine validation and communal spiritual elevation.
